arxiv-1704-03243.title: Natural convection above circular disks of evaporating liquids
arxiv-1704-03243.creator: Benjamin Dollet, François Boulogne
arxiv-1704-03243.description: Abstract We investigate theoretically and experimentally the evaporation of liquid disks in the presence of natural convection due to a density difference between the vapor and the surrounding gas. From the analogy between thermal convection above a heated disk and our system, we derive scaling laws to describe the evaporation rate.

arxiv-2112-12041.title: Gravitational Wave Imprints of Left-Right Symmetric
arxiv-2112-12041.description: Abstract We study the gravitational wave imprints of left-right symmetric model equipped with universal seesaw mechanism allowing for the natural generation of hierarchical masses of the Standard Model fermions. The scalar sector of this model is the minimal one, consisting of only two Higgs doublets.

arxiv-2212-12176.title: Detection of Solar Filaments using Suncharts from Kodaikanal Solar Observatory Archive Employing a Clustering Approach Journal: ApJ IDL, Python, Open-CV, Numpy, Pandas
arxiv-2212-12176.creator: Aditya Priyadarshi, Manjunath Hegde, Bibhuti Kumar Jha, Subhamoy Chatterjee, Sudip Mandal, Mayukh Chowdhury, Dipankar Banerjee
arxiv-2212-12176.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aditya Priyadarshi, Manjunath Hegde, Bibhuti Kumar Jha, Subhamoy Chatterjee, Sudip Mandal, Mayukh Chowdhury, Dipankar Banerjee. With over 100 years of solar observations, the Kodaikanal Solar Observatory (KoSO) is a one-of-a-kind solar data repository in the world. Among its many data catalogs, the ‘suncharts’ at KoSO are of particular interest. These Suncharts (1904-2020) are coloured drawings of different solar features, such as sunspots, plages, filaments, and prominences, made on papers with a Stonyhurst latitude-longitude grid etched on them.

arxiv-2408-07692.title: On the Parameter Selection of Phase-transmittance Radial Basis Function Neural Networks for Communication Systems
arxiv-2408-07692.creator: Jonathan A. Soares, Kayol S. Mayer, and Dalton S. Arantes
arxiv-2408-07692.description: Abstract In the ever-evolving field of digital communication systems, complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs) have become a cornerstone, delivering exceptional performance in tasks like equalization, channel estimation, beamforming, and decoding. Among the myriad of CVNN architectures, the phase-transmittance radial basis function neural network (PT-RBF) stands out, especially when operating in noisy environments such as 5G MIMO systems.

arxiv-2501-04334.title: The effective phase space and e e -folding of the Starobinsky and extended Starobinsky model of inflation
arxiv-2501-04334.creator: Theppawan Rukpakawong, Piyabut Burikham
arxiv-2501-04334.description: Abstract For zero spatial curvature, cosmological phase space of Starobinsky and extended Starobinsky inflationary model show three apparent attractors; the fixed angle attractor in the large field limit, the final attractor representing reheating phase in the small field region, and the apparent attractor corresponding to the slow-roll condition connecting between the large-field and small-field region.

arxiv-2507-07197.title: Combining Pre-Trained Models for Enhanced Feature Representation in Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2507-07197.creator: Elia Piccoli, Malio Li, Giacomo Carfì, Vincenzo Lomonaco, Davide Bacciu
arxiv-2507-07197.description: Abstract The recent focus and release of pre-trained models have been a key components to several advancements in many fields (e.g. Natural Language Processing and Computer Vision), as a matter of fact, pre-trained models learn disparate latent embeddings sharing insightful representations.

arxiv-2601-00399.title: A weak Galerkin least squares finite element method for linear convection equations in non-divergence form
arxiv-2601-00399.creator: Chunmei Wang, Shangyou Zhang
arxiv-2601-00399.description: Abstract . This article develops a weak Galerkin least-squares (WG–LS) finite element method for first-order linear convection equations in non-divergence form. The method is formulated using discontinuous finite element functions and does not require any coercivity assumption on the convection vector or reaction coefficient.

pmc-11690268.title: EXPLORING CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERSHIPS TO UNDERSTAND DISASTER PREPAREDNESS FOR OLDER AND VULNERABLE POPULATIONS
pmc-11690268.creator: Leah Haverhals, Lindsay Peterson
pmc-11690268.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As disasters continue to increase in frequency and disproportionately impact older adults and other vulnerable populations, more directed focus is needed to facilitate cross-disciplinary partnerships to better support and encourage disaster preparedness and response for these groups. Gerontologists and social scientists have opportunities to partner with engineers, geologists, demographers, epidemiologists, and other community partners to best address gaps in disaster preparation and response in research and practice.

pmc-12094100.description: PurposeSilicone mouth swabs have emerged as a promising alternative to gauze, sponge brushes, and soft-bristled toothbrushes, offering a balance between gentle cleaning and effectiveness.
